subject: Weekly Fleet Planning: capacity commitments & GPU pool sizing for upcoming deals
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Park <emma@cloudbroker.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Weekly fleet planning: Optima & other committed starts (action items)

Team —

Quick note ahead of Wednesday's planning sync. We have a handful of deals in flight that require dedicated capacity planning and finance sign‑offs. Optima Health (RDW-2026-084) is the highest priority — procurement expects a delivery window starting 2026-03-15 in their MOP. They requested an explicit GPU mapping and committed machines in the contract.

High-level ask: can infra confirm what we can guarantee for a Mar 15 start (and what is realistic if we push to Apr 1)? Finance needs committed monthly spend to put into the invoice template, and sales needs the final machine spec to lock into the contract.

A few details / constraints: 
- Optima wants isolation (dedicated pool per customer) and 99.9% uptime SLA for inference.
- Target workload: steady-state 250 tokens/sec avg, peaks to 1k tokens/sec for 30–90s bursts; model is a 70B LLM (optima-v1), expected to run in 8-bit quantized A100 or H100.
- Proposal in attachment (optima_capacity_request_20260215.pdf) includes their preferred config: 8x A100-80GB equivalents (with KV cache sizing), plus a 20% burst buffer.

Concrete asks before Wed 10:00 PT: 
1) Marissa — possible/provision timeline and recommended GPU type (A100 vs H100) and whether we need a reserved burst pool.
2) Sergio — lead time & ops runbook for bringing a dedicated pool online; any infra blockers if we pick H100s.
3) Michael — provisional committed monthly cost for 8x A100 (and for H100) including infra amortization and license fees; also guidance on buffer (20% vs 50%).
4) Evelyn — confirm contract start dates you can sign to and any procurement asks Optima raised that change sizing.

I attached the latest Q1 forecast (forecast_q1_v2.csv) — it includes pipeline-to-commit mapping for the next 90 days. Please annotate any numbers that change so we can produce a final commit/PO table for legal + procurement.

Thanks — see you on Wed.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Park <emma@cloudbroker.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 13:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet planning: Optima & other committed starts (action items)

Thanks Karthik —

Preliminary answers below after a quick pass with the ops team. I'll expand in the sync.

1) GPU recommendation: H100s give materially better latency for 70B models at 8-bit quant, especially for burst workloads. If budget is tight, 8x A100-80GB is feasible but expect ~15–25% higher per-token latency on long sequences. For guaranteed SLA and headroom, I recommend 6x H100 (as these provide more throughput per GPU) + a 2-GPU burst pool (H100) to handle spikes. Equivalent performance to 8x A100 but with smaller rack footprint.

2) Provision timeline: if we already have H100 capacity in our pool and can repurpose, provisioning the dedicated virtual pool (networking, isolation, RBAC, KV cache warmup) takes ~5 business days. If we need to purchase/allocate new H100 machines into our fleet, lead time is ~4–6 weeks. For A100s, repurposing is faster (~3 business days) but additional performance tuning is required.

3) Ops runbook notes: KV cache prewarm is critical for Optima's latency SLOs. We'll need to seed common prompt prefixes ahead of cutover — Ops will need a final prompt set from Optima. Also recommending a canary route (10% traffic) for first 72 hours.

I'll attach a short ops checklist in the drive folder. For Wed: I'll present a sizing comparison (6x H100 + 2 burst vs 8x A100) with cost delta.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet planning: Optima & other committed starts (action items)

All —

Thanks for the context. High level finance position: we can support a March 15 committed start only if sales converts the PO by Feb 25 and accepts the following: 
- Minimum 12-month committed term for dedicated pool purchases (we amortize setup costs)
- 20% minimum buffer charged as reserved capacity unless Optima signs up for burst billing (higher per-token)

Cost delta (very rough arith): 
- 8x A100-80GB dedicated pool: $86k/month (includes amortized infra + support + network licensing)
- 6x H100 + 2x H100 burst (total logical 8 H100 equivalent): $114k/month (premium for newer hw & priority scheduling)

If Optima wants lower upfront MRR we can structure a 24-month term with lower monthly amortization; I'll prepare two invoice sketches and drop them to the Drive (proposed_billing_schedule.xlsx).

One ask for Infra/Ops: if provisioning needs vendor procurement (new racks), finance needs a vendor estimate and payment terms by Friday 2/20. Otherwise repurposing existing capacity is favored.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Optima Procurement <procurement@optimahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet planning: Optima & other committed starts (action items)

Hi Karthik / Evelyn —

Thanks for the update. Confirming Optima is comfortable with a 12-month committed term and the March 15 target; procurement will attempt to get the PO signed by Feb 24. A couple of clarifications: 

- We prefer H100s if Redwood recommends them for performance; we do not expect to negotiate heavily on that point.
- We need a runbook excerpt describing the isolation layer and key rotation policies for our security team (SOC2 audit).
- Billing: Optima prefers monthly invoices with net-30 payment terms. If there is a discount for prepay/annual we can discuss that in parallel.

I'll upload a short prompt-set doc to the shared drive this afternoon so Ops can start KV warmup.

Regards,

Jillian Yates
Sr. Procurement Manager | Optima Health
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet planning: Optima & other committed starts (action items)

Quick summary post-sync and action list for clarity: 

Status: 
- H100 preference accepted (Marissa confirmed performance). We have spare H100 capacity in us-west-2 that can be repurposed; no new hardware procurement required for a Mar 15 start if PO by Feb 25.
- Ops checklist and canary plan in Drive (see link). KV warmup requires Optima prompt set by Feb 28 to hit latency SLOs on day 1.

Action items (owners / deadlines):
- Karthik: secure Optima PO by Feb 25 (sales) — if missed, default delivery moves to Apr 1.
- Evelyn: finalize contract with 12-month commitment + net-30 billing, include H100 specification and burst pool clause — due Feb 23.
- Marissa: prepare deployment runbook and capacity toggle for 10% canary & 100% cutover plan — due Feb 27.
- Michael: finalize invoice templates for both 12- and 24-month amortization options and provide cost impact to legal — due Feb 20.
- Optima: upload prompt set for KV warmup — due Feb 28.

Attachments in Drive: forecast_q1_v2.csv (annotated), proposed_billing_schedule.xlsx, ops_canary_checklist.md

If everyone agrees, I'll mark the ticket green and reserve the H100 nodes pending PO. Otherwise flag blockers by EOD tomorrow.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
